newsitem.title: NORWAY: U.S. growth data strips gains from Norwegian bonds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. growth data strips gains from Norwegian bonds.

text.p: Norwegian long bonds ended down on Wednesday after a stronger start following surprisingly strong U.S. growth in the first quarter.
The market tracked Germany and the 10-year yield spread against Bunds held at a steady 30 points.

Long bonds had come under pressure in early trade after the Norwegian crown weakened on a newspaper report quoting a study by the government department Statistics Norway. The spread against Bunds moved out to 32 to 33 points.

The study -- a mathematical model published last year -- looked at the impact of the oil producers' group, the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), on the oil market and the effect on the market of the group disbanding.
Daily Financial Dagens Naeringsliv said the break up of OPEC could reduce the value of Norway's oil assets by 70 percent, or 770 billion crowns.
"It was a completely hypothetical study. The market over-reacted," said one dealer.
Buyers returned to long debt following the brief downturn and the yield spread returned to the 30-point mark.
Meanwhile the crown stood at 4.1085 against the mark at 1400 GMT against 4.1015 at the same time a day ago.
The Norwegian Labour Directorate released a day early unemployment for April at 3.4 percent, the lowest level since 1988.

"These were very strong figures. A lower number of unemployed means higher pressure on wage increases. There is greater danger of overheating the economy when the labour market tightens," John Eriksen, I.D.E.A. Scandinavia analyst, said.
